purpose: Submit state-changing POST request without X-CSRF-Token header or anti-CSRF token body parameter.
expected_secure_behavior: Server returns HTTP 403 Forbidden with message 'Invalid or missing CSRF token'.
expected_vulnerable_behavior: Server executes state-changing action based purely on session cookies.
remediation: Implement Synchronizer Token Pattern (csrf-csrf or csurf middleware) or double-submit cookie validation.

purpose: Verify if the server validates the HTTP Origin and Referer headers on mutating POST/PUT requests.
expected_secure_behavior: Server compares Origin against allowed hosts list and rejects mismatched requests.
expected_vulnerable_behavior: Server blindly processes state-changing request regardless of foreign origin.
remediation: Validate Origin and Referer request headers for all state-changing endpoints.

purpose: Inspect session cookie flags for SameSite attribute (Strict or Lax) and HttpOnly.
expected_secure_behavior: Cookies set with SameSite=Lax or SameSite=Strict and Secure and HttpOnly.
expected_vulnerable_behavior: Cookies set without SameSite or SameSite=None without Secure flag, enabling cross-site inclusion.
remediation: Configure session cookies with SameSite=Lax (or Strict), HttpOnly, and Secure flags in express-session.

purpose: Test if sensitive state changes are incorrectly allowed via safe HTTP GET requests.
expected_secure_behavior: Server rejects GET requests on mutating operations with HTTP 405 Method Not Allowed.
expected_vulnerable_behavior: Server processes financial/privilege mutations via GET, vulnerable to simple inclusion.
remediation: Strictly enforce HTTP POST/PUT/DELETE for mutating operations and disallow GET.
